instruction: You are a strategic corporate innovation advisor conducting a reassessment. Analyse the prior assessment summary, changes since last assessment, and updated survey, then respond with a complete reassessment JSON including score_delta, carry_forward, progress, and comparison_to_previous.

answers.companyDescription: EdTech startup providing an AI-powered math tutoring platform for middle and high school students. Adaptive problem generation based on individual knowledge gaps. 30,000 active student users across 200 schools. Evaluating natural language step-by-step solution explanation and automated curriculum alignment. Multi-department organization with formalized budgets, quarterly business reviews, and a dedicated strategy function. We have invested in core systems (ERP, CRM, HRIS) but these are not always well-integrated. Innovation is a standing agenda item at board level with annual investment allocated, but execution velocity varies across business units.
answers.pastInitiatives: We experimented with a customer self-service portal two years ago after seeing competitors offer similar functionality. We built an MVP with an external agency in 3 months, but customer adoption was disappointing — only 8% of customers created accounts. We did not invest enough in understanding whether our specific customer base actually wanted self-service before building.
answers.strategicGoals: Our core business is stable and cash-generative, but we see limited growth potential within our current market. We are actively exploring adjacent business models — potentially a marketplace, a subscription-based service layer, or a data monetization play built on the proprietary data we already collect. We are willing to incubate 2-3 experimental business lines with seed funding to test viability.
answers.additionalContext: Preparing for Series A in the next 9 months. We need to articulate a clear, credible innovation strategy that differentiates us from competitors in the eyes of VCs. The narrative must tie our innovation investments directly to defensible competitive advantages and revenue growth projections.

input.changes_since_last: Major competitor entered our market. Customer churn rising. Need to accelerate digital transformation.

opportunities.title: Data & User Journey Mapping for Self-Service V2
opportunities.rationale: The initial self-service portal failed due to poor discovery, not execution. Before committing funding to a new build, the focus must pivot to deep qualitative research (data mining of existing proprietary data) and defining clear customer pain points related to knowledge gaps or administrative tasks. This validates user need before product design.

first_actions: Conduct 20+ structured interviews with high-churn customers and key educators.
Map the current student/teacher journey through the platform, identifying system handoff points (the 'process' gaps).
Build a Minimum Viable Dataset (MVD) to test hypotheses regarding self-service utility.
execution_plan.success_metric: Documented User Journey Map and validated list of top 3 high-value self-service features.
milestones: Go/No-Go recommendation for V2 MVP Scope (End of Quarter)

opportunities.title: Marketplace/Subscription Model Feasibility Assessment
opportunities.rationale: The strategic priority is diversification. This initiative must move beyond mere ideation to a structured viability assessment that mimics VC due diligence. The goal is defining the initial market segments, pricing models (subscription vs. transaction fee), and identifying necessary data infrastructure changes.

first_actions: Identify 3 distinct potential buyer personas for adjacent services (e.g., tutoring add-ons, curriculum providers).
Develop a preliminary financial model analyzing subscription revenue streams vs. marketplace commission rates.
Conduct competitive analysis on successful niche EdTech marketplaces to define necessary differentiation.
execution_plan.success_metric: Detailed Market Opportunity Report with 3 quantifiable business case options.
milestones: Presentation to Board recommending a path for incubation funding (End of Quarter)

next_steps.action: Initiate a comprehensive systems integration audit focusing specifically on data flow between CRM/ERP and the innovation pipeline to eliminate process silos.

Formalize a dedicated 'Innovation Execution Charter' defining clear decision gates, required artifacts (e.g., validated user stories, cost/benefit analysis), and accountability metrics for all future experimental initiatives.
Execute targeted retention campaigns utilizing the data insights from the initial churn analysis, focusing on high-value customers whose usage patterns indicate risk.

key_weaknesses: Core systems (ERP, CRM, HRIS) remain poorly integrated, creating operational process bottlenecks and limiting data utility.
Lack of a standardized innovation execution framework means that while funding is available, the speed and rigor of transition from idea to product are inconsistent.
Reliance on 'informal conversations' over structured, quantitative market research limits the credibility needed for Series A investor narratives.

improvements: Digital Maturity increased to Level 3 (Demonstrated investment in core systems).
Innovation is now a standing agenda item at the Board level with allocated annual funding.
Strategic focus on diversification has been formally established.
persistent_gaps: The process gap remains; funds are available, but the methodology for scalable execution and integration is underdeveloped.
Customer self-service adoption remains a weak point, indicating fundamental misalignment between perceived need and built functionality.
System silos hinder end-to-end customer lifecycle understanding.
achieved_milestones: Established formal board oversight for innovation efforts.
Increased digital maturity capacity by implementing core systems (ERP/CRM/HRIS).

comparison_to_previous.key_changes: Significant structural improvements noted (board commitment, digital capacity) and a clear strategic pivot toward diversification, compensating for initial setbacks in MVP adoption.
